title: Explainable regression guides laboratory tests of malaria candidates
summary: Piecewise-regression models learned activity relationships from 386 Open Source Malaria compounds and prioritized fragments for a commercial-library search. Researchers tested 22 selected compounds and followed three in concentration-response and human-cell cytotoxicity assays. A02 and A10 showed qualitatively consistent parasite-growth inhibition across the initial screen and follow-up curves. The third candidate, A22, has an unresolved screen-versus-curve discrepancy. These are modest-potency laboratory starting points, without established treatment efficacy or secure strongest-hit and selectivity claims.
ai_technology: modSAR supervised piecewise linear regression; SHAP
organization: King's College London; London School of Economics and Political Science; London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine; University College London

evidence.tested: Twenty-two model-prioritized commercial compounds underwent direct parasite-growth screening. A02 and A10 showed consistent qualitative inhibition across screen and follow-up; the paper additionally reports A22 concentration-response and human-cell cytotoxicity measurements, with its conflicting screen result retained.
evidence.unknown: Clinical efficacy, mechanism and independent replication are unestablished. A 22 shows only 18.6% mean inhibition at 10 micromolar in the initial screen despite a later reported IC 50 of 8.29 micromolar; the discrepancy is unresolved, so exact potency and selectivity are not represented as secure estimates.
evidence.ai_role: The fitted model learns fingerprint breakpoints and region-specific activity coefficients, prioritizing fragments and predicting activity to narrow 934 commercial compounds to 97, then 22 after additional chemical filters.

source_review.scope: Primary author-institution-deposited published version read through indexed PDF text for Methods, fragment-to-test selection, experimental results and front metadata; matched third-party journal-PDF figure inspected separately, with access distinction and numerical inconsistency retained. Current PubMed notice metadata checked.
